text:
maya: CI red on `publish-image` after my Dockerfile tweak (added a small chown in the final stage). build job fails with 401 when pushing manifest, unsure if this is my change or flakes. logs: `PUT /v2/redwood/app/manifests/latest 401 Unauthorized`

jen: can you paste the job URL + a short log block? also, which runner (kaniko / buildx) is used in CI for that job?

maya: job -> https://ci.redwood/internals/12345 (artifact attached). We're using buildx (docker buildx build --push). log snippet:```
# step push
Uploading manifest for redwood/app:latest
Error: failed to push to registry: unexpected status: 401 Unauthorized
```

tom: @maya quick sanity: did the registry credential secret rotate? CI uses ephemeral tokens with 6h TTL; if the job was queued a long time it can expire between auth and manifest finalize. ops-sre recently rotated the broker creds last night.

infra-bot: [automated] registry-credentials-rotation executed by ops-sre at 2024-06-21T02:12:00Z — affected: ci-builder pool. Rotation ID: rot-20240621-09

ops-sre: confirming rotation happened. We updated broker and CI secret store. Should be immediate but there was a short window where runners still had old tokens cached.

jen: if that's the case, easiest triage: rerun the failed job (fresh runner/token). @ops-sre can you also check `kubectl get secret regcred -n ci` on the runner namespace and share age?

ops-sre: ran `kubectl get secret regcred -n ci -o jsonpath='{.metadata.creationTimestamp}'` — created 2024-06-21T02:15:12Z (few mins after rotation). We also restarted the builder pool pods at 02:20.

maya: I retried the pipeline twice; first rerun -> same 401, second rerun started ~30m later -> still 401. Not sure why a fresh runner gets old token.

tom: hmmm. Two other possibilities: (1) the Dockerfile chown changed layer ordering and invalidated cache causing a different build cache path that the registry rejects (weird), or (2) there's a proxy in front of registry doing auth caching and returning stale 401 for some IPs.

jen: can you try one local reproduce (with your machine) to confirm it's not CI-specific? Command:```
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker buildx build --push --platform linux/amd64 -t registry.redwood.com/redwood/app:triage .
```
Include `--no-cache` to force new push: `--no-cache`.

maya: tried locally with `--no-cache` and got the same 401 on `PUT /v2/.../manifests`. But using `docker push` after `docker build` (separate auth step) worked — weird.

tom: that is interesting: buildx does the push at the end using an in-process auth token. `docker push` uses your docker daemon credential helper. Maybe the buildx ephemeral token path is hitting the stale proxy. Can you run `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.com/redwood/app:triage` to see auth handshake details?

maya: skopeo output shows `error: Error reading manifest: unauthorized: authentication required`.

ops-sre: checking registry logs for the PUT timestamp. Found a pattern: certain client User-Agent `docker/buildx` from a subset of builder IPs got a 401 followed by `auth broker returned 403` from our proxy. Looks like our broker returned a short-lived error while rotating. I can forward the proxy logs.

jen: while ops-sre digs in, quick workaround: try pushing to the staging registry host (stable host) that bypasses the proxy: `registry-staging.redwood.com` — or try forcing buildx to use docker daemon (`--load`) and then `docker push` which uses the local credential helper.

maya: tried `--load` then `docker push` to `registry.redwood.com` — success. So the image itself is fine. Looks like buildx->push path is hitting proxy/broker flaky window.

tom: root cause likely not your Dockerfile. But we still saw manifests fail in CI, so action items: (1) ops-sre to patch proxy to treat 5xx/temporarily failing broker responses as retryable for buildx user-agent, (2) infra: add a pre-publish auth check step in CI to validate token before build finishes, (3) add a CI job label to force fresh token fetch right before push.

ops-sre: ack. I'll add a short-term proxy rule this morning to retry on broker timeout for `docker/buildx` UA and follow up with a durable fix.

jen: for this PR specifically, @maya can either (A) rerun CI after ops-sre patch, or (B) change job to build+load+push with daemon helper as temporary workaround. Which do you prefer?

maya: I'll rerun after ops-sre confirms proxy change. If it still fails I'll switch the job to load+push in the PR.

ops-sre: proxy rule applied. Please rerun when ready.

maya: reran pipeline @1719004550 — job succeeded. pushing follow-up: I'll update our CI docs with a note about buildx flaky window and add a small retry in the publish step. Also opening a short follow-up ticket to add a pre-publish token check and monitor on broker errors.

tom: thanks for the quick triage team. small follow-ups: add monitor alert if >3 manifest 401s in 5min and document `--load && docker push` workaround.

ops-sre: created ticket INFRA-492: "buildx push transient 401s during credential rotation" and assigned to ops-sre; will include logs and mitigation plan.

maya: noted. closing thread for now :thumbsup:
